title: Project 02 - Herbal honey based syrup for colorectal diseases.
abstract: Our preventative measure consists of a honey-based syrup containing the powerful anti- cancerous agents i.e. apigenin in from chamomile leaves, thymoquinone (TQ) from Nigella Satvia and curcumin from turmeric. Apigenin has been demonstrated to show broad anti-cancer effects in various types of cancers, including colorectal cancer. This flavone inhibits cancer cell proliferation by triggering cell apoptosis, inducing autophagy and modulating the cell cycle. Apigenin also decreases cancer cell motility and inhibits cancer cell migration and invasion. TQ is anti-neoplastic and pro-apoptotic against colon cancer cell line HCT116. TQ is considered as potent anti oxidant, anti-carcinogenic and anti-mutagenic agent.Curcumin reduces a cancer related anti inflammatory compound PEG-2 by 60% which is a pathway strongly linked to tumor growth.

title: Project 03 - ChitoShield: Bio-Absorbable Antimicrobial Biopolymer Film
abstract: Bacterial infections and excessive fluid loss represent two major complications in topical wound management. Conventional synthetic wound dressings often rely on non-biodegradable materials and synthetic chemical additives. This project proposes ChitoShield (alternative proposed designations: PhytoDerm, BioMatrix), an eco-friendly, bio-absorbable antimicrobial biopolymer patch engineered from natural chitosan and active plant essential oils (Thymol and Eugenol). By leveraging the native electrostatic antibacterial properties of chitosan combined with essential oil-driven flexibility and enhanced antimicrobial potency, ChitoShield delivers a non-synthetic, breathable alternative for advanced wound care.

title: Project 05 - Formulation and Quality Assessment of a Triple-B Vitamin (B6, Folate, and B12) Chewable Gummy Delivery System.
abstract: Detailed Project Objectives: Formulation Optimization: Establish a robust pectin-based gel matrix capable of encapsulating active B vitamins while maintaining structural integrity, ideal elasticity, and desirable mouthfeel. Enzyme-Active Bioavailability: Incorporate methylated and activated forms of Vitamin B6 (P-5-P), Folate (L-5 MTHF), and Vitamin B12 (Methylcobalamin) to ensure maximum systemic absorption without requiring hepatic pre-activation. Quality & Stability Assurance: Prevent acid-catalyzed degradation and thermal inactivation of heat-sensitive B-vitamins by optimizing process temperature, pH windows (pH 3.2 – 3.5), and moisture levels (15% – 18% water content). Taste Masking & Sensory Compliance: Mask the characteristic metallic and bitter notes of concentrated B vitamins using natural acids, sweeteners, and citrus/berry flavors to ensure high consumer acceptability

title: Project 07 - Protein Shield: A Dual-Action Panthenol-Based Hair & Scalp Mist for Dandruff Care
abstract: Protein Shield is a lightweight, leave-on hair and scalp mist formulated to provide moisturizing, conditioning, and dandruff-care benefits. The formulation contains panthenol (Vitamin B5) as the main conditioning and moisturizing ingredient, along with glycerin as a humectant and rose water as the aqueous component. Salicylic acid is incorporated as the dandruff-care active, while sodium citrate and citric acid are used for pH control. Phenoxyethanol is added as a preservative, and distilled water serves as the vehicle. The formulation is designed to provide a refreshing, non-greasy mist that helps improve hair softness, moisture retention, and manageability while supporting scalp care. The prepared formulation can be evaluated for appearance, pH, homogeneity, sprayability, conditioning effect, moisture retention, and stability.

title: Project 09 - A Simplified Ionic Polyelectrolyte Powder for Hemostasis and Absorbent Gelation
abstract: Commercial hemostats such as fibrin sealants (e.g., TachoSil) are effective but costly, require refrigerated storage, and depend on animal- or plasma-derived proteins. By pairing two naturally derived, biocompatible polysaccharides — alginate and chitosan — with a simple ionic crosslinker, AC-Ca offers a low-cost, shelf-stable, and reproducible alternative built from standard laboratory reagents alone. The project also reinforces core pharmaceutics concepts, including polyelectrolyte complexation, ionic gelation, and rational excipient selection.

title: Project 11 - Biochemical Trigger-Based Drug-Release Prototype
abstract: This project focuses on developing a biochemical trigger-based drug-release prototype that responds to changes in environmental pH. Methylene blue will be used as a model drug, while sodium alginate and chitosan will form the polymeric matrix. Calcium chloride will act as a cross-linking agent, and glycerin will be incorporated as a plasticizer. Distilled water will be used as the solvent, while phosphate, acidic, and basic buffers will provide controlled pH conditions for evaluating the prototype. The prepared formulation will be exposed to different pH environments to observe changes in its physical properties, stability, swelling behavior, trigger response, and drug-release profile. The project aims to demonstrate the basic principle of pH-responsive drug delivery through a simple laboratory-based prototype.

title: Project 12 - DEVELOPMENT & BIOCHEMICAL EVALUATION OF FAST DISSOLVING ORAL STRIPS FOR SAFE PEDIATRIC TEETHING RELIEF
abstract: Primary tooth eruption usually begins around six months of age and continues through 24 months. During this period, infants experience localized tissue trauma, gingival erythema, and hypersalivation. Traditional pediatric oral delivery systems (e.g., suspensions and drops) frequently suffer from poor dose uniformity due to spitting or spilling. Furthermore, regulatory bodies (such as the US FDA) have issued strict warnings against conventional teething gels containing Benzocaine due to lethal systemic side effects. Fast-Dissolving Oral Strips (FDOS) provide an innovative platform to address these limitations. Placed directly on the tongue or buccal mucosa, the ultra-thin polymer matrix dissolves rapidly upon contact with saliva, releasing the active pharmaceutical ingredients instantly into the systemic circulation or locally at the gingival site without the risk of airway obstruction (choking).

title: Project Group 1 - Integrated Biochemical Assessment of Water Pollution: Relationship Between Biochemical Oxygen Demand, Heavy Metal Contamination, and Physicochemical Parameters in Local Water Bodies
abstract: Water bodies receiving domestic wastewater, industrial discharges and agricultural runoff can experience simultaneous organic and inorganic contamination. This proposal develops a more advanced biochemical assessment than a routine BOD or heavy-metal survey by integrating biochemical oxygen demand (BOD5), dissolved oxygen (DO), physicochemical characteristics, selected nutrients and trace metals. Sampling will be structured along a pollution gradient—preferably an upstream/reference location, one or more potentially impacted locations, and a downstream location—with repeat sampling across two contrasting seasons where feasible. The study will test whether increased organic loading is associated with oxygen depletion and whether heavy-metal concentrations co-vary with BOD, conductivity, turbidity and other indicators. Laboratory measurements will be subjected to quality-control procedures, descriptive statistics, correlation analysis and, where sample size permits, ANOVA or two-way ANOVA. A metal pollution index may also be calculated using applicable guideline values. The final outcome will provide an integrated biochemical picture of local water quality and identify priority parameters and sites for further monitoring.

The expected result is that refrigeration slows vitamin C degradation significantly.

title: Project Group 3 - Formulation evaluation and in vitro characterization of Transdermal Caffeine Hydrogel
abstract: This study focuses on the formulation and in vitro characterization of TransCaff™ Hydrogel, a caffeine-loaded transdermal hydrogel designed as an alternative topical delivery system. Caffeine will be obtained from a natural source such as tea or coffee and incorporated into a Carbopol-based hydrogel. The developed formulation will be evaluated for its physicochemical properties, including appearance, homogeneity, pH, consistency, spreadability, and stability. In vitro drug release and membrane permeation studies will further assess the release and movement of caffeine from the hydrogel under controlled laboratory conditions. The study aims to establish preliminary evidence for the suitability of caffeine hydrogel as a convenient, simple, and potentially cost-effective transdermal delivery system.

title: Project Group 4 - Design, Synthesis, and Quality Control Analysis of Lab-Synthesized Creatine Monohydrate
abstract: Design, Synthesis, and Quality Control Analysis of Lab-Synthesized Creatine MonohydrateThis project focuses on the laboratory-scale synthesis and quality control analysis of lemon-flavoured Creatine Monohydrate. The synthesis involves preparation of sarcosine from glycine and formaldehyde, production of cyanamide from calcium cyanamide, and reaction of these intermediates under controlled conditions to produce Creatine Monohydrate. The final product will be purified, dried, milled, and flavoured using food-grade lemon essence and stevia. Quality and purity will be evaluated through melting point, TLC, and HPLC testing. The project aims to demonstrate a cost-effective laboratory approach for producing high-purity, flavoured Creatine Monohydrate.

title: Project Group 5 - Development of a Paper-Based Colorimetric Biosensor for Non-Invasive Salivary Glucose Detection
abstract: Diabetes management requires frequent glucose monitoring, yet invasive blood sampling remains a major barrier to patient compliance. This research presents a non-invasive, paper-based colorimetric biosensor designed for the rapid detection of salivary glucose. By utilizing a specific enzymatic reaction—coating high-grade filter paper with Glucose Oxidase and a chromogenic dye—we offer a needle-free, cost-effective alternative to traditional glucometers. This project aims to bridge the gap between high-tech diagnostics and affordable healthcare solutions, specifically addressing the high prevalence of diabetes in Pakistan.

title: Project Group 6 - Awareness of Ozempic and Its Adverse Effects: A Questionnaire-Based  Study
abstract: Ozempic (semaglutide) is a GLP-1 receptor agonist mainly used for the  management of type 2 diabetes. It works by activating GLP-1 receptors, increasing cAMP signaling, and promoting glucose-dependent insulin release. Although its mechanism and common adverse effects such as nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and constipation are well established, some emerging safety concerns require further investigation. These include a possible association with non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION) and reported cases of kidney injury. However, current evidence does not establish a direct causal relationship.  This study will combine a review of recent scientific literature with an original questionnaire-based survey. The survey will assess participants’ awareness of Ozempic, its medical uses, common adverse effects, and emerging safety concerns. The collected data will be analyzed using percentages and graphs and compared with current scientific evidence. The study aims to identify gaps in public understanding of Ozempic and its adverse effects.

title: Project Group 8 - Design of a Clot-and-Heal Biodegradable BioPatch for Advanced Wound Repair in hemophilic patient
abstract: Hemophilia is a hereditary bleeding disorder characterized by deficiencies in coagulation factors, resulting in prolonged bleeding and delayed wound healing. This project proposes the development of a biodegradable multilayer bioactive wound patch incorporating bacterial cellulose, chitosan, collagen, hyaluronic acid and encapsulated clotting Factor. The patch is designed to provide localized hemostatic support, reduce infection risk, and promote skin regeneration through controlled release of therapeutic agents. The biodegradable scaffold maintains an optimal wound environment while gradually degrading after tissue repair. Physical, biochemical and drug-release characteristics of the patch will be evaluated to determine its potential as an adjunctive wound-management strategy for hemophilic patients. The proposed platform integrates biomaterials science, pharmaceutical technology and tissue engineering to create an innovative next-generation wound dressing.

title: Project - 1(Group A)- Analytical Evaluation of Drug Stability and Degradation profile in a Herbal Sunscreen Formulation
abstract: This study will be conducted to further evaluate the stability and degradation profile of a previously formulated herbal sunscreen using natural ingredients such as zinc oxide, shea butter, carrot seed oil, tulsi oil, coconut oil, and aloe vera gel. The aim is to investigate the stability of the formulation and monitor possible degradation of its UV-protective components during storage. The developed formulation previously demonstrated satisfactory physicochemical properties, including good homogeneity, spreadability, suitable pH, and acceptable appearance and texture. The formulation also showed an SPF value of approximately 13, indicating moderate UV protection. In the present study, analytical evaluation will be performed to assess changes in the formulation during defined storage conditions, with emphasis on drug content, stability, and degradation behavior. Appropriate analytical techniques will be used to identify and evaluate possible degradation of the active UV-protective component. The study is expected to provide information regarding the stability profile and quality of the herbal sunscreen and establish a basis for determining its suitability throughout the intended storage period.

title: Project - 10(Group J)- Comparative Evaluation of Aqueous Oat Extract and Methanol as Solubilizing Media for Fluconazole Using UV-Visible Spectrophotometry
abstract: Methanol is commonly used as a solvent in pharmaceutical UV-Visible spectrophotometric analysis; however, its toxicity and environmental hazards have encouraged the search for safer and more sustainable alternatives. The present study aims to evaluate aqueous oat extract as a natural alternative medium for the UV-Visible spectrophotometric determination of fluconazole. Fluconazole will be prepared at a concentration of 10 µg/mL using methanol and aqueous oat extract separately. Methanol and oat extract will be used as their respective blanks, and the absorbance of fluconazole solutions will be measured at the experimentally determined λmax. The analytical response obtained in the natural medium will be compared with that obtained using methanol based on mean absorbance and percentage difference. The study will also assess the ability of oat extract to adequately dissolve fluconazole at the selected concentration. This approach may provide a simple and environmentally friendly alternative to conventional organic solvents for pharmaceutical spectrophotometric analysis.

title: Project - 2(Group B)- Development and Characterization of Chitosan-Coated Caffeine-Loaded Collagen Nanoparticles and Evaluation of Their Cytotoxic Effects on Normal Human Fibroblast Cells
abstract: Caffeine is a widely used bioactive compound with potential therapeutic and pharmacological applications; however, its physicochemical properties and rapid release may limit its effectiveness in certain delivery systems. Nanoparticle-based drug delivery offers a promising approach for improving drug incorporation, stability, and controlled release. The present study aims to develop and characterize chitosan-coated caffeine-loaded collagen nanoparticles and evaluate their cytotoxic effects on normal human fibroblast cells. Collagen nanoparticles will be prepared using an appropriate nanoparticle fabrication technique and loaded with caffeine, followed by surface coating with chitosan to enhance nanoparticle stability and surface characteristics. The developed nanoparticles will be characterized for particle size, polydispersity index, zeta potential, morphology, drug loading, and encapsulation efficiency. In vitro release studies will be performed to investigate the release behavior of caffeine from the developed formulation. The cytotoxic effects of the nanoparticles on normal human fibroblast cells will be evaluated using an appropriate in vitro cell viability assay, with comparison to suitable controls. The study is expected to provide information regarding the physicochemical characteristics, drug-release behavior, and biocompatibility of chitosan-coated caffeine-loaded collagen nanoparticles. The findings may contribute to the development of a potentially safe and effective nanoparticle-based delivery system for caffeine and provide a basis for further investigation of its pharmaceutical and biomedical applications.

title: Project - 4(Group D)- Quality Control Assessment of Commercial Magnesium Oxide Supplements Using Complexometric EDTA Titration
abstract: Magnesium oxide is widely used in commercially available dietary supplements, making the quality and consistency of these products important for ensuring appropriate magnesium intake. This study aims to assess the quality of commercially available magnesium oxide supplements using a simple and cost-effective complexometric EDTA titration method. Selected commercial magnesium oxide tablet samples will be analyzed following acid dissolution to release magnesium ions, which will subsequently be quantified by titration with standardized EDTA solution. The determined magnesium content will be used to evaluate the assay of the products and assess variation among individual tablets and commercial preparations. The experimental findings will also be compared with the declared information on the product labels where applicable. Statistical analysis will be performed to evaluate the consistency and reliability of the obtained results. The study is expected to provide an accessible approach for the quality assessment of magnesium oxide supplements using analytical techniques suitable for a university laboratory.

title: Project - 7(Group G)- Comparative In-Vitro Evaluation of Marketed Antacid Tablets Based on Acid Neutralizing Capacity, Disintegration time and Neutralization Profile.
abstract: The present study aims to comparatively evaluate selected marketed antacid tablets based on their acid neutralizing capacity, disintegration time, and in-vitro acid neutralization profile. Commercially available antacid formulations will be analyzed under standardized laboratory conditions. Acid neutralizing capacity will be determined using a back-titration method, while disintegration testing will be performed according to pharmacopeial guidelines. The in-vitro acid neutralization profile will be assessed by monitoring pH changes in a simulated acidic medium over a specified time period. The findings of this study are expected to provide insight into the comparative performance of different marketed antacid formulations and establish the relationship between dosage-form characteristics and acid-neutralizing effectiveness. The results may contribute to the evaluation of product quality and support evidence-based comparison of commercially available antacid tablets.

title: Project - 8(Group H)- Development of Stability-Indicating UV Spectrophotometric Method for Comparative Estimation of Naproxen Sodium and Sumatriptan Succinate in Two Marketed Brands Synflex-M and Sumoxen Under Forced Degradation Conditions as per ICH
abstract: Background/Rationale* Synflex-M and Sumoxen are pharmaceutical formulations containing Naproxen Sodium 500 mg and Sumatriptan Succinate 85 mg per tablet, used in the treatment of migraine. Accurate estimation of both active pharmaceutical ingredients is important for maintaining the quality, strength, and stability of these formulations. A simple UV spectrophotometric method can provide a cost-effective approach for their simultaneous determination and stability assessment. *Objectives* The main objective of this project is to develop and validate a stability-indicating UV spectrophotometric method for the simultaneous estimation of Naproxen Sodium (500 mg) and Sumatriptan Succinate (85 mg) in two marketed brands, Synflex-M and Sumoxen. The study will determine their λmax at approximately 276 nm for Naproxen Sodium and 228 nm for Sumatriptan Succinate, compare the drug content of both marketed brands, evaluate assay and degradation, and establish the method's accuracy and precision. *Proposed Methodology* Standard solutions of Naproxen Sodium and Sumatriptan Succinate will be prepared in methanol and scanned from 200–400 nm to determine their maximum absorption wavelengths. Calibration solutions of 5, 10, 15, 20, and 25 ppm will be analyzed at 276 nm and 228 nm, and calibration curves will be prepared. The concentrations of both drugs will be calculated using the simultaneous equation method. Forced degradation will be performed using 0.1 N HCl, 0.1 N NaOH, 3% H₂O₂, and thermal treatment at 80°C. The method will then be evaluated for linearity, accuracy, precision, % assay, % degradation, LOD, and LOQ according to ICH Q1A and Q2(R1) guidelines. *Expected Outcomes/Significance* The study is expected to develop a simple, accurate, precise, and economical UV spectrophotometric method for the simultaneous determination of Naproxen Sodium 500 mg and Sumatriptan Succinate 85 mg in Synflex-M and Sumoxen. Although these drugs have previously been studied together, limited information is available on the comparative UV spectrophotometric evaluation of these two specific marketed brands under forced degradation conditions. The distinctive aspect of this project is the direct comparison of Synflex-M and Sumoxen using the same validated UV method, along with forced degradation under acidic, alkaline, oxidative, and thermal conditions. This will allow comparison of their assay, drug content, and degradation behavior, providing a broader assessment of their quality and stability for routine quality-control evaluation.

title: Project 12, Development and Characterization of an Insulin-Loaded Polymer-Lipid Hybrid Nanoformulation for Enhanced Thermal Stability in Resource-Limited Tropical Settings.
abstract: Nanoparticle (PLHN) system. By encapsulating insulin within a solid lipid core protected by a chitosan-modified shell, we aim to prevent the thermal denaturation and fibrillation of the peptide. 3. Introduction  •    The Problem: High ambient temperatures lead to insulin "unfolding" (fibrillation), reducing its efficacy and potentially causing immune reactions. •    The Goal: To design a nano-carrier that shields insulin from heat-induced mechanical and chemical stress. 4. Objectives: •    Synthesize insulin-loaded nanoparticles using biocompatible polymers (e.g., Acetylated Inulin or Chitosan) and lipids (e.g., Stearic acid). •    Evaluate the Encapsulation Efficiency (EE) and particle size distribution. •    Measure insulin stability at 37C and 45C over a 90-day period. •    Conduct in vivo studies to compare the glycemic control of the nanoformulation vs. standard insulin.

title: PROJECT 1: Group A :Liposomal Adjuvant Strategy Using Calcium disodium EDTA to Enhance Azithromycin activity
abstract: ABSTRACT:  Azithromycin is currently one of the few effective oral therapies against microbial infections, however, its reduced susceptibility high light the urgent need for innovative strategies to restore antibiotic efficacy. Recent studies have demonstrated that ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA) and its derivatives can act as effective antimicrobial adjuvants. Ca-EDTA has been shown to enhance antibiotic activity through membrane permeabilization and synergistic interactions with antibiotics such as gentamicin (Hasan et al., 2018). Additionally, EDTA has been reported to reverse antimicrobial resistance in Gram-negative bacteria through multiple mechanisms, including inhibition of efflux pumps, disruption of lipopolysaccharide (LPS) structure, reduction of biofilm formation, and modulation of resistance-associated gene expression (Aboelenin et al., 2021; Anari et al., 2022; Deilamani et al., 2023). Further evidence suggests that EDTA-based combinations can significantly enhance antibiotic efficacy through multi-mechanistic approaches, including resistance gene suppression and increased oxidative stress within bacterial cells (Hamoud et al., 2014). Moreover, advanced drug delivery systems incorporating EDTA, such as liposomal formulations, have demonstrated improved drug loading, controlled release, and reduced toxicity (Song et al., 2014). Together, these findings support the potential of EDTA as a multi-functional adjuvant capable of enhancing antibiotic effectiveness.

title: PROJECT 2: Grpoup B: Design and Optimization of Gastroretentive Floating Extended-Release Matrix Tablets of Diclofenac Sodium Using Dual Polymer System
abstract: Abstract:  Oral drug delivery remains the most preferred route due to its convenience and patient compliance. However, drugs with short half-life and limited gastric residence time often exhibit reduced therapeutic efficacy. Gastroretentive drug delivery systems (GRDDS), particularly floating drug delivery systems (FDDS), have been developed to overcome these limitations by prolonging gastric retention time and enabling controlled drug release. Floating systems are designed to remain buoyant in gastric fluid due to their low density, allowing the drug to be released slowly over an extended period. These systems are especially useful for drugs with narrow absorption windows or those requiring prolonged gastric residence. Diclofenac Sodium is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) with a short half-life (1–2 hours) and requires frequent dosing. This makes it an ideal candidate for the development of a floating sustained-release system to improve bioavailability and patient compliance. Previous studies have demonstrated that floating matrix tablets formulated using hydrophilic polymers such as HPMC and gas-generating agents like sodium bicarbonate can achieve prolonged gastric retention and controlled drug release. Additionally, the combination of hydrophilic and hydrophobic polymers has been shown to effectively regulate drug release kinetics and enhance sustained release behavior.
technologies: Hydrodynamically balanced low-density floating matrix for sustained gastric retention
Rule-based & machine-learning clinical decision support algorithm for pediatric/geriatric dosing

title: PROJECT 4: Group D: FORMULATION OF PROBIOTICS AND ZINC GUMMIES
abstract: ABSTRACT :   The formulation of probiotics and zinc gummies combines beneficial live microorganisms with an essential mineral to support gut health and immunity. Probiotics help restore intestinal microflora, while zinc enhances immune function and maintains gut integrity, creating a synergistic therapeutic effect. The synergistic effect arises because probiotics improve gut microbial balance and enhance nutrient absorption, while zinc strengthens immune defense, promotes mucosal healing, and reduces the duration and severity of infections such as diarrhea. Together, they provide enhanced therapeutic benefits compared to individual administration. Gummies are selected as a dosage form due to improved palatability, ease of administration, and enhanced patient compliance, particularly in pediatric populations. Compared to conventional dosage forms like tablets and capsules, gummies overcome issues such as swallowing difficulty and poor adherence. The formulation includes gelling agents, sweeteners, probiotic strains, and zinc salts. A major challenge is maintaining probiotic viability, which is addressed through advanced techniques like microencapsulation, controlled temperature processing, and incorporation of stabilizers such as prebiotics.

title: PROJECT 6: Group F: Formulation of Nutraceutical Jellies with ABC (Apple, Beetroot, Carrot) Juice extract
abstract: ABSTRACT:  The growing demand for patient-friendly dosage forms has encouraged the development of innovative drug delivery systems such as medicated Jellies . This study aims to formulate and evaluate Jellies incorporating ABC juice extract (apple, beetroot, and carrot), known for its rich nutritional and antioxidant profile. The objective is to develop a palatable, stable, and functional nutraceutical formulation suitable for improved patient compliance, especially among pediatric and geriatric populations. The Jellies formulation will be prepared using gelling agents such as gelatin or agar, along with sweeteners, flavoring agents, and standardized ABC juice extract. The prepared gummies will be evaluated for physicochemical properties including texture, pH, uniformity of weight, moisture content, and stability under different storage conditions. Additionally, sensory evaluation will be conducted to assess taste, color, and overall acceptability. The incorporation of ABC juice extract is expected to provide added health benefits due to its antioxidant, hematinic, and immune-boosting properties. This study highlights the potential of Jellies as an effective and appealing delivery system for nutraceuticals and functional ingredients. The findings may contribute to the advancement of patient-centric dosage forms in pharmaceutical and nutraceutical research.

title: PROJECT 7: Group G: Formulation and Evaluation of Herbal Effervescent Granules Containing Cranberry and Pomegranate Peel Extract for Urinary Tract Health.
abstract: ABSTRACT: Urinary Tract Infections (UTIs) remain one of the most frequent bacterial infections encountered in clinical practice, particularly among women in Pakistan. While conventional management relies heavily on synthetic broad-spectrum antibiotics, growing antimicrobial resistance demands effective, natural, and patient-compliant prophylactic alternatives. This project introduces the formulation, wet granulation manufacturing, and characterization of novel herbal effervescent granules combining Cranberry (Vaccinium macrocarpon) dry extract and Pomegranate (Punica granatum) peel extract. Cranberry proanthocyanidins prevent uropathogenic bacterial adhesion, while pomegranate peel provides synergistic antibacterial and antioxidant support. Developed using an optimized sodium bicarbonate and organic acid (citric and tartaric acid) effervescent couple, the granules dissolve rapidly in water (< 2.5 minutes) with vigorous effervescence, producing a refreshing mint-cranberry beverage at an ideal urinary-supportive pH (5.5–6.5). This dosage form successfully eliminates the poor palatability and slow dissolution of crude herbal powders, offering a commercially viable, industrial-scale alternative.

title: PROJECT 8: Group H: Development and Evaluation of a Medicated Chewing Gum for Preventive Oral Healthcare in Pakistan
abstract: ABSTRACT: Oral diseases represent a major but neglected public health burden in Pakistan. According to the WHO Global Oral Health Report (2022), approximately 90% of Pakistanis suffer from dental disease, with over 50 million annual cases of dental caries. Periodontal disease affects ~70% of adults over 35. The oral healthcare system in Pakistan is largely treatment-focused rather than preventive, compounded by a severe shortage of dental professionals in rural areas (1 dentist per 50,000 people) and high treatment costs (PKR 2,000–10,000 per visit). Existing preventive measures such as toothbrushing and mouthwash require consistent effort and behavioral compliance, which is often poor, particularly in pediatric and rural populations. Medicated chewing gum (MCG) is an innovative drug delivery platform that leverages the natural chewing reflex to deliver active ingredients directly at the site of action. MCG stimulates salivary flow, enhances drug distribution across oral mucosa, and enables sustained local release making it an ideal passive, effortless, and affordable oral healthcare intervention.

title: PROJECT 9: Group I: Comprehensive Quality Assessment and Standardization of a Polyherbal Tablet Formulation for IgE-Mediated Allergic Atopic Dermatitis
abstract: ABSTRACT:  To comprehensively evaluate the pharmaceutical quality and stability of the optimized polyherbal tablets through assessment of their physicochemical characteristics, mechanical properties, disintegration, dissolution, and selected chemical and stability parameters. Atopic dermatitis is a chronic inflammatory skin condition associated with hypersensitivity and immune-mediated responses. In the previous phase of this research, an in-house polyherbal formulation comprising Pterocarpus santalinus, Santalum album, Foeniculum vulgare, Elettaria cardamomum, Cordia myxa, and Artemisia absinthium was developed for the management of IgE-mediated allergic atopic dermatitis. The formulation was initially developed as a herbal syrup and subsequently optimized into a 700 mg polyherbal tablet using suitable pharmaceutical excipients. However, successful formulation development alone does not establish the quality and stability of the finished dosage form. Therefore, further pharmaceutical quality evaluation and stability assessment are required to determine whether the optimized tablets maintain their physical, chemical, and performance characteristics during storage.

title: PROJECT NO 4: Assessment of Community Pharmacists’ Knowledge and Practices Regarding Rational Antibiotic Use and Antimicrobial Resistance
courseTitle: Pharmacy Practice – IB (Introductory Pharmacy Practice Experience)
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a major global health threat driven largely by the irrational use of antibiotics. Community pharmacists are often the first point of contact for patients seeking antibiotics, so their knowledge and dispensing practices directly influence the spread of resistance. Phase 1 of this project covers the planning stage of a cross-sectional, questionnaire-based study to assess community pharmacists’ knowledge and practices regarding rational antibiotic use and AMR. During this phase a literature review was completed, study objectives and eligibility criteria were defined, the sample size was planned, and a structured questionnaire with four sections (demographics, knowledge, practices, and barriers) was developed. The questionnaire will undergo content validation by faculty and a pilot test before it is used in Phase 2.
technologies: Rule-based & machine-learning clinical decision support algorithm for pediatric/geriatric dosing

title: PROJECT NO 5: Assessment of Polypharmacy, Drug-Drug & Drug-Food Interactions, and Awareness Among Geriatric Patients, and Impact of Educational Awareness Cards
courseTitle: Pharmacy Practice – IB (Introductory Pharmacy Practice Experience)
abstract: The global demographic shift toward an aging population has led to a marked increase in geriatric patients (≥ 60 years) managing multiple long-term, co-morbid conditions—most notably hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, osteoarthritis, and chronic cardiovascular diseases. Consequently, complex multidrug regimens are routine, frequently resulting in polypharmacy (defined as the simultaneous administration of five or more medications). Polypharmacy significantly amplifies the physiological burden on elderly patients. Due to age-related pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic changes—such as decreased glomerular filtration rate (GFR), altered hepatic clearance, and reduced gastric acid secretion—geriatric patients exhibit heightened vulnerability to: Drug-Drug Interactions (DDIs) and Drug-Food Interactions (DFIs). Adverse Drug Events (ADEs) and avoidable hospital readmissions. Therapeutic Failure caused by impaired bioavailability or improper administration timing. Despite these established clinical risks, medication literacy remains critical low among elderly populations and their primary caregivers. Patients frequently lack sufficient guidance regarding administration timing relative to meals, dietary contraindications, and potential interactions with common beverages, nutritional supplements, or over-the-counter agents.

title: PROJECT NO 6 : Assessment of Polypharmacy and Medication-Related Problems in Hospitalized Patients: A Pharmacist-Led Medication Review and Counseling Approach
courseTitle: Pharmacy Practice – IB (Introductory Pharmacy Practice Experience)
abstract: Polypharmacy and medication-related problems are common among hospitalized patients, particularly those receiving multiple medications for acute and chronic conditions. Phase 1 of this project will focus on assessing medication use among selected hospitalized patients, identifying polypharmacy and potential medication-related problems, and evaluating patients' baseline understanding of their prescribed medications. Medication profiles will be reviewed for drug–drug interactions, therapeutic duplication, dose-related concerns, and unclear indications. The findings will provide a basis for pharmacist-led counseling in Phase 2.

title: PROJECT NO.3 : Smoking-Related Mortality in Pakistan
courseTitle: Pharmacy Practice – IB (Introductory Pharmacy Practice Experience)
abstract: Tobacco smoking is an important preventable cause of disease and premature death. Long-term tobacco exposure is associated with multiple serious health conditions, including cardiovascular diseases, respiratory diseases, and several forms of cancer. Pakistan has experienced a significant burden of smoking-related diseases over several decades. However, historical information regarding deaths caused by major smoking-related conditions is distributed among different research publications, government reports, health statistics, and other sources. A systematic compilation of available historical information can help provide a clearer picture of the mortality burden associated with smoking in Pakistan. This project will therefore focus on collecting and organizing historical mortality information related to major smoking-associated diseases. The major conditions considered in this project will include lung cancer, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), ischemic heart disease, stroke, and other diseases with established associations with tobacco smoking.

title: Project # 02 Surfactant Interface Modulation in Medicated Dentifrices: Formulation and Rheological Stabilization of an Antiplaque Oral Gel Using a Mixed Anionic/Non-Ionic System
abstract: • Purpose of the Study: Traditional commercial antiplaque dentifrices rely heavily on a 100% concentration of aggressive anionic surfactants like Sodium Lauryl Sulfate (SLS). Clinical data proves that raw SLS triggers significant mucosal irritation and worsens bleeding gums in gingivitis patients. This study targets a solution by modulating the surfactant interface using an ultra-mild, plant-derived vegetable co-surfactant blend to maximize phase stability and mucosal biocompatibility. • Methodology: A medicated hydrogel base was cross-linked using 2.5% Sodium Carboxymethylcellulose (Sodium CMC) and loaded with upcycled bioactive Phyto-APIs: Clove Oil (Eugenol) and Neem Extract. The critical structural change involved cutting the standard chemical SLS concentration by 50% and engineering a hybrid micellar matrix using an equal molar ratio of Coco-Glucoside (Non-Ionic Co-Surfactant). The finished gel was evaluated through spreadability indices, extrudability testing, and a 28-day accelerated thermal stability profiling at 40°C in a laboratory oven. • Expected Results: Rheological characterization showed that the hybrid SLS/Coco-Glucoside network successfully formed a tightly interlocked mixed-micellar trap, maintaining ideal thixotropic loops under shear stress. Most notably, the co-surfactant blend reduced water bleeding at the tube nozzle to 0% (Complete Syneresis Suppression) across all thermal variations, whereas standard single-surfactant control formulations exhibited phase separation and heavy thinning. • Conclusion: Surfactant interface modulation via co-surfactant engineering represents a highly innovative, scalable method to manufacture premium, low-irritation medicated oral gels. This research successfully proves that modifying interfacial tension profiles can optimize the physical stability of natural volatile oils without causing tissue toxicity.

title: Project # 03 EMULSION TYPE IDENTIFICATION STATION-Investigating the Role of HLB Value in Emulsion Type and Stability
abstract: Emulsions are commonly used in pharmaceutical formulations and are made by combining two liquids that do not normally mix, such as oil and water. An emulsifying agent is used to help form and stabilize the system. One useful way of understanding the behavior of an emulsifier is through its Hydrophilic-Lipophilic Balance (HLB) value. This project will demonstrate the relationship between the HLB characteristics of an emulsifier, the type of emulsion formed and its physical stability. Two model emulsions will be prepared using Tween 80 and Span 80. The emulsions will then be identified as oil-in-water (o/w) or water-in-oil (w/o) using a water-soluble dye test and an electrical conductivity test. The prepared emulsions will also be observed over time for visible signs of physical instability, such as creaming and phase separation. The main purpose of the project is to turn the HLB concept into a simple, hands-on experiment through an Emulsion Type Identification Station, where the relationship between emulsifier selection and emulsion behavior can be seen directly.

title: Project # 04 Development and Evaluation of a Nanostructured Lipid Carrier–Loaded Topical Gel for Enhanced Drug Delivery and Improved Diabetic Wound Healing
abstract: Diabetic foot ulcers heal slowly because of persistent inflammation, oxidative stress, excess matrix metalloproteinase activity and impaired angiogenesis. Curcumin acts on several of these pathways, but its use is limited by very low aqueous solubility, rapid degradation at the neutral to alkaline pH typical of chronic wounds, photosensitivity and poor tissue delivery. This study aims to develop and optimize a curcumin-loaded nanostructured lipid carrier (NLC) incorporated into a Carbopol gel, and to test whether it protects curcumin and releases it more slowly than a conventional curcumin gel under simulated wound conditions.

title: Project # 05 Development and Characterization of an Aspirin-Loaded Bilayer Fast-Dissolving Oral Film
abstract: The purpose of this study is to formulate and evaluate a dual-layer fast-dissolving oral film containing aspirin as a convenient oral drug-delivery system. Fast-dissolving oral films are thin, flexible dosage forms designed to rapidly disintegrate or dissolve in saliva, reducing the need for water during administration. The study will compare a conventional single-layer film with a proposed dual-layer film to determine whether the additional layer provides a useful functional enhancement. The first layer will be designed mainly for rapid wetting and disintegration, while the second layer will provide a functional/mucoadhesive feature intended to increase oral-mucosal contact. The films will be prepared using suitable film-forming polymers, a plasticizer, and other approved excipients through a laboratory-approved casting method. A suitable pharmaceutical-grade mint flavour may be incorporated to improve palatability and help mask unpleasant taste. The prepared films will be evaluated for appearance, thickness, weight variation, folding endurance, surface pH, moisture content, disintegration/dissolution behaviour, and mucoadhesive properties where applicable. Mechanical properties may also be assessed if suitable facilities are available. The expected result is a uniform, flexible film with rapid disintegration and acceptable physical and functional properties. Conclusion: The study will determine whether the proposed dual-layer architecture can maintain rapid disintegration while adding an intended functional/mucoadhesive feature compared with a conventional single-layer film.

title: Project # 06 Assessment of Antibiotic Usage Patterns, Misuse, and Awareness of Antimicrobial Resistance Among Young Adults
abstract: Antibiotic misuse has become a significant public health concern, particularly among young adults, and is one of the major factors contributing to the development of antimicrobial resistance (AMR). This study aims to assess antibiotic use, misuse, and awareness of antimicrobial resistance among young adults. A structured questionnaire-based survey will be conducted to collect information about participants’ antibiotic-use practices, including self-medication, sources of antibiotics, reasons for antibiotic use, adherence to prescribed treatment, use of leftover antibiotics, and discontinuation of treatment before completion. The study will also evaluate participants’ knowledge and understanding of antimicrobial resistance and the appropriate use of antibiotics for bacterial and viral infections. The collected data will be analyzed to identify common patterns of antibiotic misuse and determine the level of awareness regarding AMR among young adults. The findings of this study may help identify gaps in knowledge and inappropriate antibiotic-use practices and may contribute to the development of effective educational strategies for promoting responsible antibiotic use and reducing the risk of antimicrobial resistance

title: Project # 07 Bempedoic Acid in Lecithin–Tween 80 Nanoemulsions: Interfacial Characterization, Thermodynamic Modeling, and Dissolution Enhancement
abstract: Bempedoic acid is an oral ATP-citrate lyase inhibitor used to lower LDL cholesterol. It is a lipophilic dicarboxylic acid that is practically insoluble in water and in aqueous media below pH 5 but dissolves readily at pH 8, which places it in the BCS Class II range with strongly pH-dependent solubility. Acidic gastric conditions are therefore the limiting environment for dissolution, and a liquid dosage form is not currently available. This project proposes an oil-in-water nanoemulsion stabilized by a mixed Polysorbate 80 (Tween 80) and lecithin interfacial film to keep bempedoic acid solubilized in the oil core and to assess its expected release behavior

title: Project # 08 Anti-Onion Eye-Tear Protective In-Situ Gel
abstract: Onion cutting commonly causes eye irritation and excessive tearing due to the release of volatile sulfur-containing compounds that stimulate the sensory nerves of the eyes. This project aims to develop an Anti-Onion Eye-Tear Protective In-Situ Gel, a novel ophthalmic formulation designed to provide a temporary protective barrier on the ocular surface during onion cutting. The formulation is intended to be administered as eye drops and undergo in-situ gel formation upon contact with the ocular environment, allowing prolonged retention and uniform coverage of the eye surface. The proposed formulation may incorporate suitable mucoadhesive and gel-forming polymers to enhance ocular residence time and comfort. The developed gel will be evaluated for parameters such as pH, viscosity, gelling capacity, clarity, sterility, stability, and ocular retention. The formulation may offer a convenient and potentially effective approach for reducing onion-induced ocular irritation and excessive lacrimation while maintaining patient comfort. Further laboratory and safety studies would be required to establish its efficacy and suitability for human use
